Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM HST Sat Nov 07 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Pena, located several hundred miles south-southeast of the
Big Island of Hawaii.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Pena (CP4/CP042026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...PENA PROCEEDING WESTWARD... As of 5:00 AM HST Sat Nov 07 the center of Pena was located near 11.4, -153.3 with movement W at 13 mph. The minimum central pressure was 998 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 50 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Pena Public Advisory Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Sat Nov 07 2026 
000
WTPA34 PHFO 071436
TCPCP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Pena Advisory Number   4
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP042026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Sat Nov 07 2026
 
...PENA PROCEEDING WESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...11.4N 153.3W
ABOUT 1145 MI...1840 KM ESE OF JOHNSTON ISLAND
ABOUT 550 MI...885 KM SSE OF SOUTH POINT HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...998 MB...29.47 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Pena was 
located near latitude 11.4 North, longitude 153.3 West. Pena is 
moving toward the west near 13 mph (20 km/h) and this general motion 
is expected  to continue over the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Gradual strengthening is expected to occur during the next few days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 998 mb (29.47 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Mahoney

item.title: Tropical Storm Pena Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Fri Nov 06 2026 
000
WTPA44 PHFO 070840
TCDCP4
 
Tropical Storm Pena Discussion Number   3
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP042026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Fri Nov 06 2026

The latest satellite imagery indicates that Pena has re-developed
convective banding closer to the cyclone's center. In addition, a 
just-received GMI overpass suggests that the low-level structure 
has become better defined, with the possible formation of a small 
inner core.  Satellite intensity estimates have generally nudged 
upward a little since the last advisory, and based on this trend 
the initial intensity is increased to 45 kt. The latest 
scatterometer overpass missed the inner core, but did show an area 
of 25-30 kt winds 60-150 n mi away from the center in the eastern 
semicircle.
 
The initial motion is westward or 275/10 kt. Pena should be steered 
generally westward for the next several days by a large low- to 
mid-level ridge to the north of the cyclone, with a west- 
northwestward motion possible near the end of the forecast period. 
The track forecast guidance is in generally good agreement with 
this scenario, although some of the models show a south of west 
motion during the 24-60 h period. The new track forecast is similar 
to the previous forecast through 72 h and is a little south of the 
previous forecast at 96 and 120 h.
 
The intensity forecast still has some confidence issues.  The
overall environment still seems to be favorable, with warm sea
surface temperatures, a moist air mass, and light shear for at
least the next four days. This results in the statistical-
dynamical guidance showing steady strengthening. However, the
dynamical model guidance is in poor agreement on how much
strengthening will occur and if there will be any strengthening at
all. To highlight the spread of just the global models, the ECMWF
shows strengthening through the next five days, the GFS and the
Canadian show little development through three days followed by
some strengthening, and the UKMET shows essentially no
strengthening at all during the forecast period.  Given the lack of
model consensus even on trends in the forecast intensities, the 
intensity forecast calls for gradual strengthening in best 
agreement with the SHIPS model. The new forecast is an update of
the previous forecast.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  07/0900Z 11.4N 152.4W   45 KT  50 MPH
 12H  07/1800Z 11.4N 153.9W   50 KT  60 MPH
 24H  08/0600Z 11.4N 155.7W   55 KT  65 MPH
 36H  08/1800Z 11.2N 157.5W   60 KT  70 MPH
